rows.title: Caterpillar and balanced species tree growth-factor conjecture
rows.record_statement:
Let $k$ be fixed and let $n$ be sufficiently large. An **unranked species tree** is a species tree considered up to isomorphism, and a **caterpillar tree** and a **balanced species tree** are, respectively, the extreme unbalanced and balanced species-tree shapes of size $k$. The ${\mathbb{D}\mathbb{L}}$-histories are histories in the duplication-loss model.

**Caterpillar and balanced species tree conjecture.** For a given $k$ and sufficiently large $n$, the unranked species tree of size $k$ having the largest number of ${\mathbb{D}\mathbb{L}}$-histories of size $n$ is the caterpillar tree. Moreover, the exponential growth factor of the number of histories for a caterpillar of size $k$ grows superlinearly as a function of $k$. Species trees having the smallest number of ${\mathbb{D}\mathbb{L}}$-histories are balanced species trees of size $k$, and the exponential growth factor of the number of histories for a balanced tree of size $k$ grows linearly as a function of $k$.

This conjecture characterizes the species-tree shapes that produce the largest and smallest numbers of duplication-loss histories for fixed species-tree size. The source presents these growth assertions as conclusions suggested by experiments; no proof or resolution is given.
rows.source: Cedric Chauve, Yann Ponty and Michael Wallner, “Counting and sampling gene family evolutionary histories in the duplication-loss and duplication-loss-transfer models”, arXiv:1905.04971 (2019).
rows.what_was_proved: For each k≥1, one cutoff N(k) works for all unranked rooted full binary k-leaf species trees: for each n≥N(k), the count of source duplication–loss event histories with n extant gene leaves is minimized exactly by the recursively leaf-balanced shape and maximized exactly by the caterpillar. Each species tree’s positive nth-root growth limit is the inverse critical radius, the caterpillar growth divided by k tends to infinity, and the balanced growth lies between 2k and 1000k for all k≥1.

rows.title: Existence conjecture for D-optimal rhombic designs
rows.record_statement:
Let $K$ be the dimension, let $D$ be the covariance matrix of the random coefficients, and let $(d_0,d_1,d_2)^T\in\mathcal{C}_K$ denote its parameter vector. A **rhombic design** is an invariant design from the class studied for the multiple linear regression model on the hypercube, and a design is **$D$-optimal** if it maximizes the determinant of its information matrix under covariance matrix $D$. **Existence conjecture.** For even $K$, there is a $D$-optimal rhombic design for all

$$
(d_0,d_1,d_2)^T\in\mathcal{C}_K.
$$

For odd $K$, there is a $D$-optimal rhombic design for all

$$
(d_0,d_1,d_2)^T\in\mathcal{C}_K\quad\text{with}\quad d_2\leq\frac{d_1}{2}.
$$

The conjecture records the observed existence pattern for $D$-optimal rhombic designs: existence was found for all parameter values in even dimensions, whereas in odd dimensions it was established only in the stated region. Whether such designs exist for all remaining parameter values when $K$ is odd is left open.
rows.source: Ulrike Graßhoff, Heinz Holling, Frank Röttger and Rainer Schwabe, “Optimality regions for designs in multiple linear regression models with correlated random coefficients”, arXiv:1911.05538 (2019).
rows.what_was_proved: For every integer K≥2 and covariance parameters d₀,d₁>0 and −d₁/(K−1)≤d₂≤d₁, if K is even or K is odd and d₂≤d₁/2, there exists a finitely supported probability design on [−1,1]^K invariant under coordinate permutations and global negation, with support on nonzero space diagonals and at most an antipodal pair on each diagonal. Its determinant for the weighted intercept-and-coordinate information matrix with variance d₀+(d₁−d₂)Σᵢxᵢ²+d₂(Σᵢxᵢ)² is at least that of every finite approximate design on the cube.

rows.title: Congruence-class bias conjecture for parts in k-regular partitions
rows.record_statement:
For $k$-regular partitions, let $D_k(r,t;n)$ denote the number of occurrences of parts congruent to $r$ modulo $t$ among the partitions of $n$. Here $t\geq 6$, $1\leq r<s\leq t$, and $k\geq 3$.

**Congruence-class bias conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$,

$$
D_k(r,t;n) \geq D_k(s,t;n).
$$

Moreover, for $k\geq 2$, if

$$
n>\max\{t+3,16\},
$$

then

$$
D_k(r,t;n)>D_k(s,t;n).
$$

The conjecture formalizes the observed bias toward smaller parts and extends the finite computational verification to all $t\geq 6$ and all admissible congruence classes. The preceding theorem establishes related bounds for $2\leq k,t\leq 10$, while the asserted ranges beyond those finite checks remain open.
rows.source: Faye Jackson and Misheel Otgonbayar, “Biases among Congruence Classes for Parts in k-regular Partitions”, arXiv:2207.04352 (2022).
rows.what_was_proved: Let D_k(r,t;n) count all occurrences, with multiplicity, of parts congruent to r modulo t among partitions of n in which each part occurs fewer than k times. For all t≥6 and 1≤r<s≤t, D_k(r,t;n)≥D_k(s,t;n) for k≥3 and n≥1, and D_k(r,t;n)>D_k(s,t;n) for k≥2 and n>max(t+3,16).

rows.title: Finiteness conjecture for connected graphs with odd metamour period
rows.record_statement:
A graph's **metamour period** is the least positive integer $k$ for which its iterated metamour graph returns to the original graph, under the metamour operation used in the paper. Let $k$ range over the positive odd integers.

**Finiteness conjecture.** For each odd $k\in \mathbb{Z}^+$, there exist only finitely many connected graphs with metamour period $k$.

The paper has already classified the connected graphs with metamour period $3$: they are $C_7$ and $C_9$. The conjecture predicts analogous finiteness for every odd period, and the classification of such graphs remains open in general.
rows.source: William Q. Erickson, Daniel Herden, Jonathan Meddaugh, Mark R. Sepanski, Mitchell Minyard and Kyle Rosengartner, “Limits and Periodicity of Metamour 2-Distance Graphs”, arXiv:2409.02306 (2024).
rows.what_was_proved: For each positive odd integer k, there exists a finite collection of connected finite simple graphs whose least positive return to the identical labelled graph under repeated distance-exactly-two adjacency is k. Every connected finite simple graph of that exact period is isomorphic to a member of the list.

closest_prior_read.citation: Erickson et al., Limits and Periodicity of Metamour 2-Distance Graphs

evidence.says: Theorem 4.1: “A graph G has metamour period 1 if and only if G is edgeless.”

rows.title: Failure of the matroid matching property in odd-dimensional rigidity matroids
rows.record_statement: For integers $k\geq 2$ and sufficiently large $n$, consider the rigidity matroid ${\mathcal R}_{2k+1}(K_n)$ of the complete graph $K_n$ in dimension $2k+1$. **The matroid matching conjecture.** The matroid ${\mathcal R}_{2k+1}(K_n)$ does not have the matroid matching property for all $k\geq 2$ and sufficiently large $n$. The preceding proof establishes the corresponding even-dimensional result, while the odd-dimensional case is suspected to fail in this way for dimensions at least five and large complete graphs.
rows.source: John Hewetson, Bill Jackson, Anthony Nixon and Ben Smith, “k-fold circuits and coning in rigidity matroids”, arXiv:2508.18838 (2026).
rows.what_was_proved: For every k >= 2 and every n >= 2(2k+3)^2 + 2(2k+3) - 1, the generic rigidity matroid R_{2k+1}(K_n) does not have the matroid matching property: an explicit family of h edge pairs has maximum matching h-2 while the Dress-Lovasz min-max bound is h-1. rows.title: Cell-count conjecture for face Schubert arrangements of polytopes
rows.record_statement: Let $P\subseteq \mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ be a full-dimensional polytope, and let $P^{[k]}$ denote its $k$-stabbing set. Consider the $k$-face Schubert arrangement of $P$ inside $P^{[k]}$, and the sign vectors determined by its defining equations for $V\in P^{[k]}\setminus \mathcal{H}_P^k$. **Cell-count conjecture.** The number of cells in this arrangement is equal to the number of sign vectors realized by such spaces $V$. This would show that, for Schubert arrangements arising from polytopes, cells are uniquely determined by their realized sign vectors; the claim is presented as an expectation, and no resolution is supplied in the source.
rows.source: Sebastian Seemann and Francesca Zaffalon, “How to stab a polytope”, arXiv:2412.00551 (2024).
rows.what_was_proved: There is a full-dimensional eight-vertex rational polytope in ℝP³ whose space of stabbing projective lines avoiding every edge-span divisor has no bijection between its connected components and the realized projective Chow sign vectors, taken modulo simultaneous sign reversal. Two lines meeting the interior share one strict sign class but lie in different components.

rows.title: Lattice-realization conjecture for preorder lattice-point posets
rows.record_statement:
Let $\tau$ be a preorder of size $n$, let $P_\tau$ be its lattice-point poset, let $M_{P_\tau}(x,y)$ be its $M$-triangle, and let $\overline{M}_{P_\tau}$ be the transmutation defined by

$$
\overline f(x,y)=f\left(\frac{1-y}{1-xy},1-xy\right).
$$

**Lattice-realization conjecture.** There exists a finite graded lattice $L_\tau$ of rank $n$ such that

$$
\mathcal Z(P_\tau,t)=\mathcal Z(L_\tau,t),\qquad \overline M_{P_\tau}(x,y)=M_{L_\tau}(x,y).
$$

In particular, the rank-generating polynomial of $L_\tau$ equals $h(\tau,t)$. The conjecture extends the arbor setting; the source gives examples for chain preorders but no general resolution.
rows.source: Frédéric Chapoton and Christos A. Athanasiadis, “Polytopes and posets associated to preorders”, arXiv:2605.26916 (2026).
rows.what_was_proved: For the three-element preorder with two incomparable minima below one maximum, no finite graded lattice of rank three has M-triangle equal to the rational transmutation of the M-triangle of the preorder polytope's lattice-point poset. This refutes Conjecture 8.1.

rows.title: The three-component-intersection extremal conjecture for odd n
rows.record_statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ with $n$ odd, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of graphs on $[n]$.

**Three-component-intersection conjecture.** If the intersection of any two graphs in $\mathcal{F}$ has at most three components, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq \frac{(n+3)^2}{8}\frac{1}{2^n}\cdot 2^{\binom{n}{2}}.
$$

For more than two components, the authors report that fixed-Hamilton-cycle constructions no longer appear optimal. For three components they suspect the bound is attained by a construction based on two half-sized cycles meeting at a point, although the displayed conjecture is the stated quantitative claim.
rows.source: Imre Leader, Žarko Ranđelović and Ta Sheng Tan, “A Note on Hamiltonian-Intersecting Families of Graphs”, arXiv:2309.00757 (2023).
rows.what_was_proved: For every h >= 1, on n = 6h-1 labelled vertices there is a family of (1+6h+12h^2)*2^(C(n,2)-6h) graphs whose pairwise intersections (including a graph with itself) have at most three components, exceeding the conjectured bound ((n+3)^2/8)*2^(C(n,2)-n); hence Leader-Randelovic-Tan Conjecture 7 fails for arbitrarily large odd n (ratio -> 4/3).

evidence.says: Theorem 2: “Then |𝓕|≤2^{binom(n,2)}/2^{n−1}.”

rows.title: Bóna's maximal-avoidance conjecture for Hertzsprung patterns
rows.record_statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}_k$ be the set of Hertzsprung patterns of length $k$, let $\tau\in\mathcal{S}_k$, and let $|\mathcal{S}_n(\tau)|$ denote the number of length-$n$ objects avoiding $\tau$. Write $\mathrm{id}_k$ for the identity pattern of length $k$. **Bóna's maximal-avoidance conjecture.** For every Hertzsprung pattern $\tau\in\mathcal{S}_k$ and every natural number $n$,

$$
|\mathcal{S}_n(\tau)|\leq |\mathcal{S}_n(\mathrm{id}_k)|.
$$

Bóna proved the inequality for non-self-overlapping patterns. The paper reports computational evidence suggesting that self-overlapping patterns also satisfy it, but gives no general proof.
rows.source: Anders Claesson, “From Hertzsprung's problem to pattern-rewriting systems”, arXiv:2012.15309 (2021).
rows.what_was_proved: For every pair of natural lengths k,n and every permutation pattern τ of length k, the number of length-n permutations avoiding τ as a consecutive block whose values are one integer translate of τ, with the empty pattern occurring at every boundary, is at most the number avoiding the increasing pattern of length k. If n>k, this inequality is strict whenever τ is neither increasing nor decreasing.

closest_prior_read.citation: Bóna, Where the monotone pattern (mostly) rules, author preprint

evidence.says: §3: “Bóna [5] showed that |𝒮ₙ(τ)|≤|𝒮ₙ(idₖ)| for each non-self-overlapping pattern τ∈𝒮ₖ.”

rows.title: The strict lower-bound conjecture for the robust clique covering number
rows.record_statement: Let $G$ be an isolate-free graph. Write $\theta(G)$ for its clique covering number and $\theta_1(G)$ for the corresponding robustness parameter, so that the general lower bound is $\theta_1(G)\geq\theta(G)$. **Strict lower-bound conjecture.** The inequality is strict unless $G$ is edgeless; equivalently, equality can occur only for edgeless graphs. This conjecture asks for a characterization of the equality case in the lower bound for the robust clique covering number. Its status is not established in the supplied source.
rows.source: Gábor Bacsó, Balázs Patkós, Zsolt Tuza and Máté Vizer, “The robust chromatic number of graphs”, arXiv:2305.01923 (2023).
rows.what_was_proved: For every finite simple graph G with at least one edge, theta_1(G) > theta(G), where theta_1(G) = max over 1-selections f of theta(G - f(V)); equivalently theta_1(G) = theta(G) iff G is edgeless (Conjecture 1 of Bacso-Patkos-Tuza-Vizer). Proved; the MathDB isolate-free hypothesis is not needed.
